cases.customer_question: Can a product be registered as LE-only when the included QDID/DN uses a dual-mode Core Controller and Core Host design?
question_variants: Can I change the ICS from dual-mode to LE-only during qualification?
How should an LE-only product be declared when the referenced design is dual-mode?
Why does the qualification workspace reject a single-mode ICS for a dual-mode included design?
Can BR/EDR be disabled in software while keeping a dual-mode qualification registration?
How do I handle LE-only products under the post-July-2024 qualification process?
cases.actual_issue: A product intended to operate as LE-only reused included QDID/DN designs that were qualified as dual-mode Core Controller and Core Host implementations. Under the newer qualification process, changing the registration ICS to single-mode creates inter-layer consistency check failures.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The product only uses LE in practice, but the Bluetooth designs it reuses were originally qualified as dual-mode. The qualification system checks whether the registration matches the included designs. If the registration is changed to LE-only while the included designs remain dual-mode, the submission can fail consistency validation.
cases.consultant_answer: When included QDID/DN entries are dual-mode Core Controller/Core Host designs, the newer qualification workflow performs stricter inter-layer consistency checks. Changing the registration ICS to LE-only or BR/EDR-only causes the submission to fail consistency validation and prevents progression to submission. The correct approach is to keep the qualification registration as dual-mode while disabling BR/EDR functionality in the product software so the shipped product behaves as LE-only.
cases.decision_logic: Qualification consistency is determined by the characteristics of the included qualified designs. A registration ICS that conflicts with the transport capabilities declared by the included dual-mode designs fails the enhanced consistency checks introduced in the newer qualification process.
cases.final_recommendation: Keep the registration as dual-mode to remain consistent with the included QDID/DN designs, and implement LE-only behavior by disabling BR/EDR in software if required by the product.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Changing the registration to a single-mode ICS can cause consistency-check failures and prevent submission completion, resulting in qualification rework and registration delays.
